reason: The finding holds as a cheap planning check. It adds no mechanism and has 0 LB or private value. (1) Its premise is verified. grep 'quota' in CONTEXT.md finds the last reading at l.2542: 07:55/30 h at 26 Sep 21:5xZ. There is no reading on 27 or 28 Sep, and neither R20-A7 nor R21-A11 landed. (2) `kaggle kernels list --mine --sort-by dateRun` (read-only, 01:25Z) shows 19 GPU runs after that reading: part of exp70g, exp70j/k, exp71 (T4x2), exp70n/q, exp72, exp76d, exp75, exp76a, exp78a, exp77 (T4x2), exp76e, exp78b, exp79d, exp79a, exp81/exp80a, and exp83a/b (01:01-01:02Z 28 Sep). The r21w-3 per-kernel times plus exp83a/b give ~12.7-14 h, so ~20.6-22 h used and ~8-9 h left. If T4x2 bills at 2x (unverified), it is ~25-26.5 h used and ~3.5-5 h left. That matches the finding's 21-26 h. The reset is Sat 3 Oct 00:00Z, after the deadline (CONTEXT l.1545). (3) Hidden reruns do not use quota (CONTEXT l.1972). So quota never blocks a submit of an already-dummied file. It blocks only new dummies, and the team rules require a dummy PASS before each W3/W4/E10 submit. Running out would therefore cost a slot. The '<3 h left' branch fires in roughly 10-20% of cases, mainly under 2x T4x2 billing. (4) Feasibility: the Kaggle API has no quota endpoint, so the read goes through the browser (Settings page, ~2 min). It is read-only, touches no kernel, no code and no submission, and has no R1-R10 or R8 implication. Why not refuted: it costs almost nothing and guards the E10 reserve. It is a repeat of R20-A7/R21-A11 only because those never landed, not because they were refuted. The r21w-3 skeptic's 'quota not binding' held at ~20 h, but the 2x-billing upper case now leaves under ~5 h, so the reading can change which dummies are pushed.
fix:
At the next browser-agent pass, and before the next dummy push, read https://www.kaggle.com/settings once (GPU quota line) and log 'GPU quota <used>/30 h at <time>' in CONTEXT.md.
Apply the thresholds on hours LEFT:
- >= 5 h: no restriction beyond the W2/W3/W4 tables.
- 3-5 h: no speculative stack dummies. Push only the tabled W3/W4 files, and keep >= 1 h for an E10 (A) dummy.
- < 3 h: push a dummy only for the chosen FULL, and keep 1 h reserved for an E10 (A) dummy.
Fallback if no reading lands before a push decision: plan with the worst case (~26.5 h used, ~3.5 h left), which means the 3-5 h rules.
Also record once whether T4x2 kernels bill at 1x or 2x: compare the reading with the ~20.6-22 h (1x) and ~25-26.5 h (2x) estimates.
No CLI or push is involved. The reading is information only and never, by itself, a trigger to submit.
realistic_gain: 0 on public LB and on private. It is insurance: in roughly 10-20% of cases (2x T4x2 billing) it prevents a W3/W4 or E10 slot from being lost because a dummy cannot run on quota at a critical hour. Cost: ~2 min of browser time.
evidence: CONTEXT.md l.2542 (07:55/30 h, 26 Sep 21:5xZ), l.1545 (Saturday 00:00Z reset), l.1972 (hidden reruns use no quota)
